lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Rebuilt the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards around per-sensor error budgets, cutting mean time to detect incidents from 40 to 12 minutes.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Add a concise target-role headline or summary.
items.because: Recruiters must infer how the robotics, ML, and agent work fit together.

items.says: Put experience in reverse chronological order, with the later internship first.
items.because: The May 2023–July 2024 role currently appears above the October 2024–May 2025 internship.

items.says: Consider placing projects before less directly relevant experience.
items.because: The projects include current work that is highly relevant to agent engineering.

items.says: Use consistent, specific location formatting.
items.because: Education and job locations mix “USA” and “Country,” unless “Country” is redaction.

items.says: Broaden the skills section with substantiated engineering and ML capabilities already shown in the bullets.
items.because: The current list is sparse and omits areas such as model serving, inference optimization, CI, APIs, and event-driven systems.

items.says: Group skills by recognizable capability.
items.because: This would help recruiters and screening systems find relevant engineering and ML skills.

items.says: Check that the portfolio link leads to relevant, accessible work.
items.because: A working link can substantiate the agent-runtime and evaluation claims.

items.says: Make the M.S. degree status unambiguous and ensure the expected graduation date is current.
Clarify what the diagnostics monitoring work covered.
items.because: Readers need to understand the scope of the impact.

items.says: Say whether the detection-time reduction was measured after deployment.
items.because: This would make the impact more credible.

items.says: Give the workload or test conditions behind the p95 values.
items.because: The measurement context is needed to interpret the latency reduction.

items.says: Distinguish the latency result from its validation method.
items.because: The result and build-failing load tests should be easy to tell apart.

items.says: “Maintained” and “adds” create a tense mismatch.
items.because: The bullet looks insufficiently proofread.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution to the CI pipeline and regression checks.
items.because: It is unclear whether you maintained an existing system, added checks, or both.

items.says: Separate or prioritize the fleet migration bullet’s many contributions.
items.because: The technical change and operational outcome are buried among library work, onboarding, and on-call duties.

items.says: Clarify whether the nightly backlog disappeared entirely or was reduced.
Define the pending-case backlog and give its comparison period or baseline.
items.because: That context is needed to interpret the 68% reduction.

items.says: Clarify your role in launching the triage system.
Describe the accuracy change as an 8-percentage-point increase.
items.because: It should not be read as an 8% relative gain.

items.says: Give before-and-after latency or define the baseline and workload.
items.because: The 40% reduction needs measurement context.

items.says: Explain the evaluation setup for “single-request” inference with dynamic batching.
items.because: The pairing may prompt questions about whether requests were concurrent.

items.says: Rewrite the awkward opening construction.
items.because: It makes the method and result harder to parse.

items.says: Clarify what you implemented in the GRPO work.
items.because: The detailed method obscures your contribution.

items.says: Specify what the 5% latency result measures and how the comparison was established.
items.because: The outcome needs to be interpretable.

items.says: Show what improved with one rollout per prompt, or make the bullet’s purpose clearer.
items.because: It describes a procedural choice without showing its effect.

items.says: Clarify the extent of your authorship of the runbook material.
Clarify whether runbook adoption was team-wide or limited to on-call reviewers.
items.because: The extent of adoption is unclear.

items.says: Replace the broad “AI-first engineering practices” claim with what you personally built or changed and a concrete outcome.
items.because: The bullet sounds generic and gives no specific contribution or measured impact.

items.says: The reduction from 900 ms to 600 ms is one-third, not 50%.
items.because: The stated percentage is mathematically inconsistent.

items.says: Ensure the metric is specifically tool-call latency rather than overall task latency.
Call the rise from 71% to 83% a 12-percentage-point increase.
items.because: The change should be distinguished from a percent increase.

items.says: State the benchmark scope and test conditions.
items.because: Readers need them to judge whether the result is robust.

items.says: Make sure “upstreamed” accurately describes your role.
Make sure the claimed default-benchmark behavior is still current.
Explain what the 0.89 correlation indicates about evaluator behavior.
items.because: Without context, readers may not know why it is meaningful.

items.says: Clarify whether you only identified and traced the defects or also helped fix them.
items.because: Your part in the upstream fixes is implicit.
